'''Victor Snieckus''' (August 1, 1937 – December 18, 2020<ref name="chemviews">{{cite web |title=Victor Snieckus (1937 – 2020) |url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/11282662/Victor_Snieckus_1937__2020.html |website=ChemistryViews |publisher=Wiley-VCH GmbH |access-date=27 December 2020 |date=21 December 2020}}</ref>) was a Lithuanian-born Canadian chemist. He was [[Emeritus|professor emeritus]] at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]]. Specializing in [[organic synthesis]], he was known for his influential research on [[directed ortho metalation]].<ref name="chemviews" /><ref name="qg">{{cite web |title=Queen's remembers Professor Emeritus Victor Snieckus |url=https://www.queensu.ca/gazette/stories/queen-s-remembers-professor-emeritus-victor-snieckus |website=Queen's Gazette |publisher=Queen's University |access-date=27 December 2020 |date=22 December 2020}}</ref><ref name="green_2001">{{cite journal |last1=Green |first1=James R |title=Biography of Professor Victor Snieckus |journal=Canadian Journal of Chemistry |date=1 November 2001 |volume=79 |issue=11 |pages=v–vii |doi=10.1139/cjc7911dedicat}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Snieckus was born on August 1, 1937, in [[Kaunas]]. During [[World War II]], his family fled to Germany, and in 1948, immigrated to [[Alberta, Canada]]. Snieckus received his bachelor's degree in chemistry from [[University of Alberta]] in 1959, his master's degree from [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1961, and his PhD from the [[University of Oregon]] in 1965 under the supervision of [[Virgil Boekelheide]].<ref name=green_2001 /> He spent a year as a [[postdoctoral scholar]] at the [[National Research Council of Canada]].<ref name=chemviews /><ref name=qg />

==Academic career==
In 1967, Snieckus joined the faculty of the [[University of Waterloo]] as an [[assistant professor]], becoming an [[associate professor]] in 1971 and a [[full professor]] in 1979.<ref name=chemviews /><ref name=qg /> He assumed the [[Monsanto]]/NRC research chair in 1992.<ref name=qg /><ref name="gunn">{{cite news |last1=Gunn |first1=Andrea |title=The magic of chemistry |url=https://www.queensu.ca/gazette/alumnireview/stories/magic-chemistry |access-date=27 December 2020 |work=Queen's Alumni Review |issue=3 |date=2019}}</ref>

Snieckus relocated to [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] in 1998, where he assumed the [[Alfred Bader|Bader Chair]] of Chemistry. He retired and became professor emeritus in 2009.<ref name=chemviews /> He founded a company, Snieckus Innovations, the same year, originally funded by [[Alfred Bader]].<ref name="cic">{{cite news |last1=Lougheed |first1=Tim |title=A synthesizing life |url=https://www.cheminst.ca/magazine/article/a-synthesizing-life/ |access-date=27 December 2020 |work=Canadian Chemical News |publisher=Chemical Institute of Canada |date=November–December 2016}}</ref> Throughout his career Snieckus consulted for the [[pharmaceutical]] and [[agricultural]] industries.<ref name=chemviews /><ref name=qg />

Among other awards, Snieckus became a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada]] in 1993, a Fellow of the [[Lithuanian Academy of Sciences]] in 1999,<ref name=green_2001 /> and a Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2009.<ref name=chemviews /><ref name=green_2001 />

Snieckus served as an editor for a variety of academic journals, was the president of the [[International Society of Heterocyclic Chemistry]] in 1985, and chaired the American Chemical Society's Organic Division in 1989–90.<ref name=green_2001 /> He co-organized an academic conference series, Balticum Organicum Syntheticum, a chemistry conference held in the [[Baltic States]].<ref name=chemviews /><ref name="bos">{{cite web |title=Organizers |url=https://boschem.eu/organizers/ |website=Balticum Organicum Syntheticum |access-date=27 December 2020}}</ref>

==Research==
Snieckus' research interests in [[organic synthesis]] focused on [[metalation]] and particularly [[lithiation]]. He is best known for his work on the [[directed ortho metalation]] family of reactions.<ref name=chemviews /><ref name=qg /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Snieckus |first1=Victor |author1-link=Victor Snieckus |title=Directed ortho metalation. Tertiary amide and O-carbamate directors in synthetic strategies for polysubstituted aromatics |journal=Chemical Reviews |date=September 1990 |volume=90 |issue=6 |pages=879–933 |doi=10.1021/cr00104a001}}</ref> His work has had practical applications in both academic and industrial settings,<ref name=green_2001 /> particularly in the industrial-scale synthesis of [[pharmaceutical]]s and in an agricultural [[antifungal]].<ref name=gunn /><ref name=cic />
